summary: While adding a public function to tabulate, the user says every public function he adds, in any repo, must carry a short >>> example that passes as a doctest (he reviews diffs on his phone). Last session adds a public function to sqlparse, whose code has no doctests anywhere, so mirroring local style gives a prose-only docstring.

turns: Can you add a public `register_format(name, table_format)` to tabulate, so we can plug in our own TableFormat without poking at `_table_formats`? The new name should show up in `tabulate_formats` as well, since the CLI's -f check uses that.

Make sure its docstring has a short >>> example that actually passes as a doctest. I want that on every public function I add, whatever the repo: I review most diffs on my phone, and one example tells me more than a paragraph of prose.

Add a top-level `sqlparse.statement_types(sql)` that returns, in order, what `Statement.get_type()` says for each statement `sqlparse.parse()` finds in the string, e.g. `['SELECT', 'INSERT']`. It's for a migration linter we're writing.

facts.text: Personal preference, any repo: every public function the user adds gets a short >>> usage example in its docstring that passes as a doctest (he reviews diffs on his phone).
